chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Bashīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim al-Ḥannāṭ asked him and said: “May Allah keep you well, I sell food to a man on deferred terms, then I come while the price of the food has changed from its price, and he says: ‘I do not have dirhams.’”

He عليه السلام said: “Take from him according to the price of that day.” He said: “I understand, may Allah keep you well, that it is my food which he bought from me?” He عليه السلام said: “Do not take it from him until he sells it and gives you [the payment].”
He said: “May Allah humble my nose; he gave me a concession, but I responded back to him, so he made it stricter for me.”

key_terms.إِلَى أَجَلٍ: on a deferred term or credit until a specified time
key_terms.الطَّعَامَ: food merchandise being sold on deferred payment
key_terms.دَرَاهِمُ: silver coin currency used for payment
key_terms.رَخَّصَ: he granted a concession or lenient allowance
key_terms.سِعْرِ يَوْمِهِ: the market price of that day at the time of settlement
key_terms.فَشَدَّدَ: he imposed a stricter ruling after further questioning
key_terms.لَا تَأْخُذْ: a prohibition against taking the item in the specified manner
key_terms.يَبِيعَ: that he sells the item first before repayment is made

ai.seo_question: Can a seller take repayment in goods at the current market price when a buyer on credit has no cash?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about settling a deferred food sale when the debtor cannot pay in cash and market prices have changed. The Imam عليه السلام permits taking value according to the current day's price, but forbids taking back the very same food sold until the buyer first sells it and then pays. It addresses fairness and legal limits in commercial dealings.
